Maya (Support): Customer reports 401s from a Dedicated deployment behind their VPC LB. They say tokens are valid and work against our hosted API, but on their private gateway calls fail. Repro steps copied below.
Maya (Support): key detail: this is a private/VPC setup using our edge proxy + CloudLB (internal). They started seeing failures after a config change to the L7 proxy last night. Impact: multiple endpoints, intermittent. Customer timeline attached: https://example.com/screencap (redacted).
Priya (Eng-Infra): Can you paste the raw curl you used for repro? Need to confirm whether Authorization header actually reaches our gateway or is stripped at the LB. Also tell me the gateway image + envoy version.
Maya (Support): Repro from customer (anonymized):
```bash
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer ey...customertoken..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  https://private-dedicated.acme.internal/v1/generate
```
Response: 401 Unauthorized, body: {"error":"invalid_token","message":"missing required claim: org_id"}
Headers returned to client: `server: envoy`, `x-request-id: 9f2a3c` (no auth debug headers)
Diego (Eng-Platform): The error message implies our authz layer received the request but the JWT claim 'org_id' was absent. Two possibilities: (1) LB or ingress rewrote Authorization into a different header or removed the token, and our token exchange path tried to use client cert fallback; (2) a different token reached the service (e.g., proxy inserted internal token). We need packet-level header traces.
Riley (SRE): Quick check: does customer use Google Internal LB or AWS NLB w/ proxy protocol? I remember GCP LB sometimes drops Authorization unless you set `preserve_external_request_headers: true` or enable passthrough. If they use Istio, outbound mTLS can also strip custom headers depending on policy.
Maya (Support): Customer says GCP ILB with an HTTP(S) proxy in front of our edge. They recently enabled the LB's CDN/MLB feature. They can repro by hitting the LB ip: 10.1.2.3 directly.
Priya (Eng-Infra): Ok reproduce attempt on our lab cluster using similar setup. Running curl to the ILB -> envoy edge. I see 401 and when I dump the request at the edge (envoy access log) the `Authorization` header is absent. LB health check path is `/hc` and we do pass-through for that.
Priya (Eng-Infra): FWIW, envoy has header sanitation by default: `envoy.filters.http.router` will remove certain hop-by-hop headers but not Authorization. The missing header suggests the HTTP(S) proxy modified it. I can reproduce by toggling the LB header rewrite: when I enable `strip_request_headers: ["authorization"]` on the proxy, header disappears and we get the same 401.
Maya (Support): Customer claims they didn't intentionally strip Authorization. Could the CDN feature be acting as an edge auth plugin and rewriting headers?
Diego (Eng-Platform): Very likely. Some CDN/edge features insert an internal ID and replace Authorization with a signed assertion for their origin auth. Check the LB request headers that reach our origin (use tcpdump or enable `xff and raw header capture`).
Riley (SRE): Suggestion: have customer run a curl to an echo endpoint we control that prints incoming headers. Example command:
```bash
curl -s -D - -o /dev/null -H "Authorization: Bearer XXX" https://private-edge.echo.internal/headers
```
That will show whether Authorization survives the LB.
Maya (Support): Customer ran that and posted results: Authorization is missing at the echo service. They also included trace of our ingress access logs showing `-` for auth header. So LB appears to strip. Customer attached ILB config screenshot.
Priya (Eng-Infra): Temporary mitigation: configure our edge proxy to accept token passed in a different header the LB preserves (e.g., `x-forwarded-authorization`) by mapping it to `Authorization` in the proxy's `http_connection_manager` request headers. Alternatively, change LB to forward `Authorization` (preferred). I'll draft a snippet:
```yaml
# envoy http_connection_manager request headers
request_headers_to_add:
  - header:
      key: "Authorization"
      value: "%REQ(X-FORWARDED-AUTHORIZATION)%"
```
This maps the preserved header into Authorization for downstream filters.
Diego (Eng-Platform): If we do header mapping ensure we validate the token signature and claims again — don't trust the LB. Also update docs so customers with ILB/CDN know to enable a passthrough or forward-header option.
Maya (Support): Customer asked if this is a security risk. They want us to confirm safe patterns.
Priya (Eng-Infra): Security posture: mapping from `x-forwarded-authorization` is acceptable only if the LB is within a trusted VPC and we require mTLS between LB and edge. If the LB is in customer's control and private, it's fine. If not, insist on passthrough. We'll coordinate with security for wording.
Diego (Eng-Platform): I'll open a docs PR and a KB article: "Private deployments: LB header preservation and Authorization passthrough".
Riley (SRE): Logging + alerting: add a metric when requests to dedicated endpoints have missing Authorization header but return 401 from auth filter. That will help detect similar incidents.
Maya (Support): Next steps for customer we executed: (1) we asked them to enable header passthrough on LB; (2) we applied a temporary proxy mapping on their dedicated gateway to accept `x-forwarded-authorization`; (3) we rotated the customer's key as precaution (they requested it). Customer confirms calls now succeed -> 200s.

deploy-bot: Deployment `edge-proxy/2026-03-15-priv-overlay` succeeded in 3 regions :white_check_mark:

Priya (Eng-Infra): I'll open an internal issue with steps to harden the gateway so that future LB/CDN configs won't silently break auth. INC-4532 created and assigned to eng-infra. Proposed tasks: docs, default passthrough config, mapping example, unit tests for header preservation.

Maya (Support): Closing loop with customer: "We've identified the LB as the cause. We've provided a temporary mapping and steps to enable passthrough. We'll follow up when platform changes are in." Customer replied :thumbsup: and will keep us posted if they re-enable CDN.

Diego (Eng-Platform): Action items: (a) PR for KB, (b) CI test that simulates ILB header rewrite, (c) consider adding an `Authorization` guard in our edge operator to warn if upstream is known to be header-stripping.

Maya (Support): Thanks all. Marking P2 for now since there's a config workaround and customer is back online. Reopen if it recurs.
